name: MBR Cookie Consent
author: Robert Palmer

sections.description: Enterprise-grade cookie consent management compliant with GDPR/EEA, UK DUAA, US CCPA and multi-state privacy laws, LGPD, PIPEDA, Quebec Law 25, Switzerland nFADP, Australia Privacy Act, India DPDP, Vietnam PDPL, Indonesia UU PDP, Nigeria NDPA, China PIPL, South Korea PIPA, Saudi Arabia PDPL, South Africa POPIA, and other global privacy regulations. Features Google Consent Mode v2, Microsoft UET Consent Mode, Global Privacy Control (GPC) signal support, automatic script blocking that stays correct behind a page cache, local consent logging, 22 community translations, WCAG 2.1 AA accessibility, settings import and export, and a built-in privacy policy generator with AI/LLM training disclosure. Completely free with no upsells and no telemetry. Nothing leaves your server on the visitor path unless you switch geolocation on.
sections.changelog:
2.3.6

  • Fix: geolocation could not work on a site behind Cloudflare. Cloudflare's country header was only trusted when the connecting address was one of Cloudflare's own, which is never true once your host restores original visitor IPs — the arrangement Cloudflare recommends and most managed hosts enable by default. On those sites the header was discarded and every visitor fell back to the default region, so a UK site could show the United States banner to everyone. The header is now also trusted when the connecting address matches the address Cloudflare reports, which is the signature of a restored-IP setup. A forged header naming somebody else's address is still rejected.
  • Fix: selecting ip-api.com without a pro key switched geolocation off entirely. Its free endpoint is plain HTTP only, and the plugin will not send a visitor IP over an unencrypted connection without an explicit opt-in — but instead of saying so it made no request at all and quietly handed every visitor the default region. Lookups now fall through to ipapi.co over HTTPS, and the settings screen explains why.
  • New: Cloudflare's country header is used automatically whichever lookup provider is selected. It costs no outbound request, cannot be rate-limited, adds no latency and sends no visitor IP to a third party. Can be turned off with the mbr_cc_prefer_cloudflare_country filter.
  • New: the True-Client-IP header is now read. It is the Enterprise-plan equivalent of CF-Connecting-IP and was previously ignored.
  • Fix: Cloudflare's Pseudo IPv4 feature broke detection. With "Overwrite Headers" selected, Cloudflare replaces CF-Connecting-IP with a Class E address and preserves the real one in CF-Connecting-IPv6. Class E is a reserved range, so the plugin rejected it and those visitors fell back to the default region. The preserved address is now used.
  • New: the Geolocation screen reports how the country was actually arrived at — Cloudflare header, your configured provider, the ipapi.co fallback, or not detected at all. A fallback is shown in amber and says plainly that it is your default region rather than a lookup result.
  • New: where a request demonstrably came through Cloudflare but the country header is absent, the screen names the Cloudflare setting to enable and where to find it. CF-IPCountry is not sent by default.
  • New: an optional "My origin only accepts traffic from Cloudflare" setting, for origins firewalled to Cloudflare's ranges or using Authenticated Origin Pulls. Off by default, and excluded from settings export — it is a fact about one server's firewall, and importing it elsewhere would turn spoofable headers into trusted ones on a site that never made that guarantee.

2.3.5

  • Fix: the "Enable WCAG/ADA Compliance Features" switch would not stay on. Ticking it and saving returned a page with the box clear again, which looked exactly like the save had failed. The setting was registered with a text sanitiser rather than a boolean one, so the screen stored the word "true" instead of a real yes/no value and the checkbox never recognised it on the way back in.
  • Fix: the same fault meant the accessibility features could not be switched off either. The stored word "false" counts as a yes in PHP, so the screen reported the setting as off while the screen-reader announcements carried on running. The switch now saves, displays and applies correctly in both directions. Existing sites are set to on when they update, which is what they were actually doing.
  • Fix: A/B testing did not work behind a page cache. The variant was chosen on the server and written into the page, so whichever visitor generated the cached copy had their variant stored in it and everyone served that copy afterwards saw the same one. Impressions were recorded against the cached variant rather than the visitor's, so the figures measured the cache rather than the test. Variants are now assigned in the browser and the page is identical for every visitor. Reset your statistics before drawing conclusions from an existing test.
  • Note: the A/B assignment cookie is no longer HttpOnly, because the script that assigns it now has to read it back. It remains a session cookie holding a single letter naming a banner layout, and no personal data.
  • Fix: promoting an A/B winner wrote an invalid banner setting. Variants B and C stored a layout name in the position setting, a combination the appearance picker cannot represent, so it showed no layout selected and the next save on that screen quietly reset it. Promotion now writes a matching position and layout, and purges the page cache.
  • Security: the consent log's visitor fingerprint is now salted. It was an unsalted SHA-256 of the visitor's IP address and browser identification string — both drawn from a small enough range that the original address could be recovered from an exported log by trying every possibility. It is now keyed with a per-site salt that never leaves the server. Rows written before this release will not match rows written after it; nothing queries the column, so nothing else changes.
  • Change: the network consent log export column is now headed "Visitor Hash" rather than "Cookie Hash". It has never been a hash of the consent cookie.
  • New: the Geolocation screen warns that IP lookup providers are third parties with their own licensing, and that free tiers are generally offered for non-commercial, testing or development use. The Cloudflare option avoids the question entirely.
  • Update: corrected the ePrivacy Regulation withdrawal date on the EU compliance card, which read February 2026. It was announced on 11 February 2025, approved on 16 July 2025 and published in the Official Journal on 6 October 2025.
  • Update: US state privacy notes refreshed to August 2026. Alabama's Personal Data Protection Act confirmed for 1 May 2027. Maryland (1 July 2026) widened "precise geolocation" to a 1,750-foot radius covering a consumer, mobile device or vehicle. Virginia (1 July 2026) prohibits selling precise geolocation outright. New Jersey (30 June 2026) bans the sale of sensitive data by any entity with no consumer-volume threshold.
  • Update: Connecticut SB 4 notes expanded for 1 October 2026, and Vermont's DPOSA carries the same AI/LLM training disclosure duty as Connecticut from 1 January 2028 — the disclosure this plugin generates now serves two states.
  • Update: Oklahoma SB 546 treats pseudonymous data as personal data wherever it can reasonably be linked to a person, bringing cookie identifiers into scope.
  • Update: India DPDP clarified — from 13 November 2026 the Data Protection Board may hear complaints, conduct inquiries and levy penalties, six months before the 13 May 2027 full compliance deadline.
  • Update: EU Digital Omnibus still in negotiation as of August 2026 with no agreed text. Nothing to reconfigure.

2.3.4

  • Fix: regional banner settings did not reach the banner. Each region carried a dozen settings and the banner read three of them, so a visitor in the UK saw much the same banner as a visitor anywhere else. The geolocation test tool did read them all, which made this hard to spot: it reported behaviour, in detail, that the banner had never implemented.
  • Fix: regional detection could show visitors the wrong region's banner. The region was decided on the server and written into the page, so on a cached site a visitor in the United States could prime the cache with a banner carrying no Reject button, which was then served to visitors in the EU. The region is now resolved in the browser.
  • Change: your own banner text now always takes precedence over a region's suggested wording.
  • Fix: the "Do Not Sell or Share" link could be shown to everyone. It was switched on from the visitor's Global Privacy Control signal while the page was being generated.
  • Fix: page exclusions did not exclude script blocking. An excluded page still had its third-party scripts held with nothing offering to release them, so a first-time visitor landing there had no way to consent at all. Excluded pages now show the floating Cookie Settings button.
  • Change: hiding the banner on a page no longer means consent stops applying there. A new setting allows third-party scripts on excluded pages for sites that need it; off by default.
  • Change: switching the banner off site-wide now switches script blocking off with it.
  • Removed: Google Additional Consent Mode. No AC String was ever generated, stored or sent; the provider list was a placeholder and the JavaScript file was never loaded. Sites that had it on get a one-time notice. Google Consent Mode v2 is unaffected.
  • Removed: Google Ad Manager from the generated privacy policy's service list, where it appeared purely because the ACM option was ticked. Regenerate your policy if you created one with ACM enabled.
  • Change: the consent cookie is now percent-encoded. Cookies written by earlier versions are still read, so nobody is asked to consent again.
  • Fix: geolocation could silently never run. The settings screen defaulted to one lookup provider while the lookup itself defaulted to another, so on sites where the geolocation screen had never been saved no lookup happened at all.
  • Fix: an unrecognised provider value fell back to the plaintext provider. It now falls back to the HTTPS one.
  • Fix: the Advanced Consent Management settings tab closed two levels too deep.
  • Fix: corrected the readme, which still advertised IAB TCF and Google ACM, claimed no external requests, described the consent cookie as HttpOnly, and named cookies that were never set.

2.3.3

  • Fix: quotes and apostrophes in banner text gained extra backslashes on every save, doubling each time — one, then three, then seven, then fifteen. Affected the heading and description, button labels, policy link text, all geolocation regional wording, category names and descriptions, blocked script details and the form integration message. Fixed at every save handler.
  • Fix: settings already damaged by that bug are repaired automatically, once, on the first admin page load after updating.
  • Note: Custom CSS is excluded from the automatic repair, because CSS uses backslashes as real escape characters. If you had quotes in your Custom CSS, check it by hand.
  • Performance: the site-wide scanner now works in batches with a wall-clock budget, so it completes on ordinary hosting instead of timing out.
  • Performance: the visitor's region is resolved once per request rather than on each of the eighteen calls that ask for it.
  • Fix: A/B counters could lose increments when two visitors arrived at once. Increments are now performed by the database and cannot be raced.
  • Fix: page exclusions could white-screen the front end — the setting defaults to a list but saves as text, and the mismatch was a fatal error on every page load once the field was used.
  • Fix: an exclusion pattern containing a bracket or plus sign produced an invalid regular expression and a warning on every page load.
  • Fix: Global Privacy Control could be applied to every visitor. The signal was read server-side and cached, so one visitor with GPC enabled suppressed marketing consent site-wide. It is now read in the browser.
  • Fix: every consent log row recorded its method as "other", making the Method column useless as compliance evidence.
  • Fix: the network consent log export wrote unescaped browser identification strings to CSV, allowing an unauthenticated visitor to plant a formula that ran when an administrator opened the file. It also loaded the whole log into memory; rows are now batched.
  • Fix: a malformed cookie category no longer causes a fatal error.
  • Removed: dead GPC filters and an unreferenced settings view.
  • New: automatic translation now works. The banner can be shown in the visitor's own language in 22 languages, chosen in the browser so the page remains cacheable. Previously this was advertised but did nothing — the translation code hung on a filter the plugin never called.
  • New: translations are community-contributed and must be approved by an administrator on the new Translations screen before any visitor sees them. Unreviewed languages fall back to your own wording.
  • Note: the supported language count was previously stated as 40+. It was 22, and remains 22 — now complete across every string rather than about half.
  • Fix: banner text you have customised is never replaced by a translation.
  • Fix: approved languages are excluded from settings export.
  • Removed: IAB TCF v2.3. The feature never worked — it sent every vendor the same fixed consent string regardless of what the visitor chose, with a CMP ID of zero and an empty vendor list. A fixed signal claiming consent is worse than sending none. Proper TCF support requires registration as a CMP with IAB Europe. Sites with the option enabled get a one-time notice.
  • Removed: the IAB TCF section of the generated privacy policy. Regenerate your policy if you created one while TCF was enabled.
  • Fix: video embeds were not blocked on sites using a click-to-play facade. Performance plugins replace the iframe with a poster image and a data attribute holding the URL, so no iframe remained for the blocker to find and the embed loaded regardless of consent. Facades are now recognised and held. If you run a video facade alongside this plugin, re-test your embeds after updating.
  • Fix: video poster images are held until consent too — a facade avoids the embed's cookies but still sent the visitor's IP address to the provider on page load.
  • Fix: script and iframe blocking is no longer decided on the server from the visitor's cookie. On a cached site the first visitor to accept could prime the cache with unblocked HTML that was then served to everyone. Every visitor now receives the same fully-blocked document and their browser releases what their own choice permits — so the plugin is safe behind a page cache.
  • Fix: an inline script matching two blocked patterns at once was wrapped twice, duplicating its blocking markers.
  • Fix: blocked embed placeholders no longer flash on screen for visitors who had consented.
  • Fix: the blocked embed placeholder stylesheet always loads, so the placeholder is no longer shown unstyled on default settings.
  • Performance: a substring test now precedes each blocking regular expression.
  • Fix: Google and Microsoft Consent Mode reported the wrong state on cached sites. The default written into each page was read from the visitor's cookie, so a consenting visitor's "granted" could be cached and served to everyone after them. Defaults now come from your settings alone; the visitor's real choice is applied in their browser before any tag loads.
  • Fix: scripts restored after consent were inserted as async and could execute out of page order.
  • Fix: the Consent Mode script block is no longer printed when both modes are disabled.
  • Fix: blocking an inline script by text pattern could delete page content. The match had no script boundary, so it could run past an earlier script's closing tag and swallow everything up to the next match — blocking the wrong script, removing the intended one, and silently deleting the markup between them. Affected sites using a custom blocked script of type "inline".
  • Fix: inline-blocked scripts carried no consent category, so all of them were treated as marketing on the front end. An analytics-categorised script stayed blocked for visitors who accepted analytics but declined marketing.
  • New: saving settings now purges the page cache, so banner changes appear on a cached front end immediately instead of looking like the save had failed. SiteGround Speed Optimizer, WP Rocket, LiteSpeed, W3 Total Cache, WP Super Cache, WP Fastest Cache, WP-Optimize, Cache Enabler, Breeze, Nginx Helper and WP Engine are supported.
  • Dev: new filters mbr_cc_flush_caches and mbr_cc_cache_ignored_options, and actions mbr_cc_before_flush_caches and mbr_cc_flush_caches_after.

2.3.2

  • New: choose the banner logo from the Media Library instead of pasting a URL. Live preview and remove button included; pasting a URL still works.
  • New: Glassmorphism toggle with Opacity and Blur sliders, applied to the banner only so the preference centre stays readable, plus a live WCAG contrast readout that tells you whether your chosen combination stays legible over any background. Automatic solid fallback for unsupported browsers and for visitors who prefer reduced transparency.
  • New: Dark Mode — off, follow the visitor's system setting, or always on. Your Accept and Reject button colours are preserved.
  • New: Preview banner button — see the banner with your current unsaved settings, at desktop and mobile widths, rendered by the real front-end renderer so it cannot drift from the live result.
  • Fix: the Media Library handler for the logo had existed in the admin JavaScript since an earlier release but was bound to a button that was never added to the template, so it never ran.
  • New: Dashboard now offers Edit and Regenerate buttons for the Privacy Policy page. Regenerating rewrites the content from your current settings while keeping the page's title, URL and published status, and saves the previous version as a revision first.
  • Fix: the update manifest required PHP 8.0 and WordPress 6.0 while the plugin supports 7.4 and 5.8, so sites on those versions were never offered updates. Corrected.
  • Fix: banner text set in the plugin was ignored on the front end when WPML was active — WPML returned its own previously registered copy instead of the updated setting. The plugin's setting now wins in the site's default language.
  • Fix: settings that only make sense on the site they were set on — the logo's attachment ID, visitor IP detection mode, trusted proxy list, the ip-api.com key, the plain-HTTP geolocation opt-in and the AI training disclosure settings — are now excluded from settings export and import. The new appearance settings (glassmorphism, opacity, blur, dark mode, logo URL) are carried as normal.

2.3.1

  • Security: forwarding headers (X-Forwarded-For, CF-Connecting-IP and similar) are no longer trusted unconditionally. Previously any visitor could set them to choose their own privacy regime, or to generate unlimited cache entries and outbound lookups. A new Visitor IP Detection setting controls this; the default validates Cloudflare's header against Cloudflare's own address ranges, so Cloudflare sites need no configuration.
  • Security: geolocation lookups no longer run over plain HTTP by default. Over HTTP the country returned can be rewritten in transit, silently changing which privacy regime visitors are shown, and visitor IPs travel unencrypted to a third party. Sites on ip-api.com without a pro key are moved to ipapi.co (free, HTTPS) and told so via a notice.
  • Security: the unauthenticated consent logging endpoint is throttled per visitor and category names are validated, so the consent log cannot be flooded or polluted.
  • Security: consent log CSV exports are protected against spreadsheet formula injection.
  • Security: the cookie scanner is restricted to your own site and no longer disables TLS verification. No outbound request disables certificate verification any more.
  • Security: the settings save handler writes only recognised settings; the consent cookie is marked Secure on HTTPS; blocked inline scripts are restored without eval(), so script blocking works under a strict Content-Security-Policy.
  • Fix: scripts blocked by src were tagged with an empty consent category, so after a visitor accepted cookies those scripts could silently fail to restore. Iframes were unaffected.
  • Fix: subdomain consent sharing failed across all of .co.uk, .com.au, .co.nz and similar suffixes — the cookie domain was computed as "co.uk", which browsers reject.
  • Fix: A/B impressions were counted on every page load rather than once per visitor, so existing statistics are overstated and worth resetting.
  • Fix: network settings whose names contained "button" were stored as booleans, so the accept, reject and customise button labels were saved as 1 instead of their text.
  • Fix: AI training disclosure settings and the geolocation cache duration were missing from settings exports.

2.3.0

  • New: "Rest of World" region now defaults to opt-in instead of implied consent. Existing sites are NOT changed — an upgrade routine preserves your current behaviour; only new installs get the stricter default.
  • New: dedicated regions for Nigeria (NDPA + GAID), China (PIPL), South Korea (PIPA), Saudi Arabia (PDPL) and South Africa (POPIA), all opt-in with localised banner headings.
  • New: AI / LLM training disclosure for Connecticut SB 1295 — the first US state law requiring your privacy notice to say whether personal data trains large language models. Includes a clear "we do not" statement option.
  • Update: Connecticut notes greatly expanded (35,000 threshold, no-threshold triggers, neural data, widened profiling opt-out, 1 Aug impact assessments, cure period removed, SB 4 on 1 Oct 2026).
  • Update: Arkansas HB 1717 and Utah HB 418 added; EDPB Binding Decision 1/2026 noted on the EU card.
  • Fix: corrected ePrivacy Regulation withdrawal dates (announced 11 Feb 2025, approved 16 Jul 2025, OJ 6 Oct 2025).
  • Fix: Canada notes no longer describe Bill C-27 as pending — it died in January 2025.
  • Fix: the Geolocation testing tool reported "Rest of World" for every region added since 2.1.0 (Vietnam, Indonesia and the new 2.3.0 regions). Live detection was always correct — only the admin test readout was wrong. It now reads the real region configuration instead of a duplicate list.

2.2.1

  • Fix: failed geolocation lookups are no longer cached for the full 24-hour duration. A provider failure (unreachable, rate-limited, or blocked) previously pinned the fallback default region to the visitor's IP for a day — and could freeze the wrong regional banner into cached pages. Fallbacks now cache for 5 minutes and self-heal.

2.2.0

  • New: Import / Export settings — download this site's configuration as a portable JSON file and import it on another install, built for multi-site rollouts. Covers banner, categories, blocked scripts, consent mode, GPC, IAB TCF, form integration and all geolocation regional text.
  • New: One-step "Revert last import" restores the previous settings.
  • Security: allowlist-driven import — unknown fields are ignored and every value is re-validated before storage.
  • Note: consent logs are never included in a settings export; site-local values (policy page IDs, IP cache) are excluded.

2.1.1

  • New: Vietnam PDPL (Law 91/2025, in force 1 Jan 2026) added as a dedicated opt-in privacy region with granular per-purpose consent and a Vietnam compliance card.
  • Update: US multi-state notes refreshed (enacted total ~24 states; CT + UT changes effective 1 Jul 2026; CA DROP broker deadline 1 Aug 2026).
  • Update: EU notes flag the Digital Omnibus proposal (Arts 88a/88b) as a forward-looking item in trilogue.

1.1.3

  • Self-hosted update support.
  • Maintenance and packaging fixes.

1.1.2

  • Appearance refinements.
sections.installation: Upload the plugin to /wp-content/plugins/ and activate.

upgrade_notice: Important if your site is behind Cloudflare. Geolocation could not work on a Cloudflare site whose host restores original visitor IPs — the setup Cloudflare recommends — so every visitor was handed the default region while the settings screen reported it as a detection. A UK site could be showing the United States banner to everyone. Also fixes ip-api.com silently disabling geolocation when selected without a pro key.
